name: Disorder of Glycolysis

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficient activity of one or more glycolytic enzymes in erythrocytes or muscle tissue
Presence of exercise intolerance, hemolytic anemia, or episodic rhabdomyolysis
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding glycolytic enzymes
Elevated serum lactate and pyruvate levels during episodes
Histological evidence of glycogen accumulation or muscle fiber necrosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Deficient glycolytic enzyme activity plus clinical features consistent with disorder and/or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may require integration of biochemical, genetic, and clinical data.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic hemolysis triggered by physical exertion
Muscle breakdown episodes often precipitated by exercise or fasting
searchTerms: episodes of muscle pain and weakness

pathognomonic.notes: Transient weakness related to impaired glycolytic energy production
searchTerms: loss of muscle strength during exercise

common.notes: Persistent tiredness disproportionate to activity level

common.symptomName: Muscle cramps during or after exercise
common.notes: Painful involuntary contractions linked to energy metabolism defects
Enlarged liver due to glycogen accumulation in some cases

occasional.notes: Yellowing of skin and eyes due to increased bilirubin
searchTerms: yellowing of skin from red blood cell breakdown
skin discoloration from blood cell destruction

occasional.notes: Rare involvement of cardiac muscle in severe cases
Low blood sugar during fasting or illness
Occasional cognitive impairment in severe enzyme deficiencies

rare.notes: Rare neurological manifestation possibly due to metabolic imbalance
Occasional nerve damage presenting with sensory symptoms
Enlarged spleen secondary to chronic hemolysis

laboratory: Reduced activity of glycolytic enzymes (e.g., pyruvate kinase, phosphofructokinase)
Elevated serum lactate and pyruvate during episodes
imaging: Muscle MRI showing edema or fatty infiltration in chronic cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding glycolytic enzymes such as PKLR, PFKM, ALDOA
other: Muscle biopsy showing glycogen accumulation and fiber necrosis
Peripheral blood smear showing echinocytes in pyruvate kinase deficiency

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent muscle cramps and myoglobinuria
Lactic acidosis not limited to exercise episodes

redFlags: Recurrent rhabdomyolysis with risk of acute kidney injury
Progressive muscle weakness leading to disability
references: Hirschhorn R, Reuser AJJ. Glycogen Storage Disease Type I: Disorders of Glycogen Metabolism. In: Scriver CR, et al., editors. The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. 2001.
